# QS-CFW-4516-94 Quality specification - connecting rod CFW-4516-94 (1045)

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-4516-94

Scope
This quality specification defines the acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for the forging and finishing of connecting rod CFW-4516-94 (CFW-4516-94) manufactured in Plant P3 from 1045 material. The document applies to all incoming forgings, in-process operations, and final functional inspections prior to release to assembly or external shipment. It covers metallurgical hardness, critical bore geometry, forging weight limits, visual and dimensional requirements where they affect fit or function, and the required records to demonstrate compliance.

Background and rationale
Connecting rod performance is controlled by core material properties and tight geometry at critical features. Hardness is used as a proxy for heat treatment and tensile properties; observed service and qualification testing require the rod to achieve a specific hardness band to ensure fatigue performance and bearing compatibility. Bore diameter tolerance is critical for journal fit and bearing clearance after machining; controlling bore tolerance at the forging stage minimizes downstream machining risk and ensures consistent wall thickness. Forging weight is controlled to manage die fill, internal soundness, and to limit defects associated with over- or under-filled impressions.

Requirements table
The following table lists the mandatory acceptance criteria for the part. These are minimum inspection limits and must be met for release.

| Characteristic | Requirement | Notes / Acceptance |
|---|---:|---|
| Hardness (through or core, as applicable) | 28-32 HRC | Measured per inspection method below. Parts outside this band are rejected. |
| Bore diameter tolerance (unmachined forging ID) | ±0.10 mm | Measure at specified inspection locations; see Inspection Method. |
| Maximum forging weight (as-forged, prior to trim) | 28.4 kg | Weigh part on calibrated scale; parts over limit are rejected and investigated. |

Inspection method
General
Inspections shall be performed by qualified personnel using calibrated instruments. Calibration certificates for measurement equipment must be retained with the inspection records. Environmental conditions that materially affect measurement must be recorded in the inspection log.

Hardness measurement
Hardness testing shall be performed on representative locations that reflect core and critical cross-section properties. Use a method appropriate to HRC scale; ensure the test impression is placed where it will not be removed in subsequent processing or affect fit. Record the reading and the measurement location. If a part yields a reading outside 28-32 HRC, perform two additional measurements at other representative locations; if any measurement remains outside the requirement, the part lot is nonconforming.

Bore diameter measurement
Measure the unmachined forging internal diameter at the bore midspan and at a near-end location to verify uniformity. Use calibrated bore gauges or a coordinate measuring device to achieve sufficient resolution. Acceptance is based on the unmachined bore being within ±0.10 mm of the nominal drawing size supplied with the part release. Document all readings, gauge identification, and operator.

Weight measurement
Weigh each forging on a calibrated industrial scale. Record the net as-forged weight and scale calibration ID. Any forging exceeding the maximum forging weight of 28.4 kg must be quarantined and evaluated for die fill issues, trimming errors, or potential internal anomalies. For lots where multiple parts exceed the limit, initiate an investigation per Nonconformance Handling.

Additional inspections and sampling
Visual inspection for surface defects that would impair fit or fatigue life shall be performed on all parts. Metallurgical sampling or nondestructive testing may be required based on prior history or when anomalies are detected during dimensional or hardness inspection. All sampling plans and subsequent results must be recorded.

Inspection records to keep
- Hardness readings with location and tester ID.  
- Bore diameter measurements with gauge/coordinate device ID.  
- Individual part weight records with scale calibration reference.  
- Visual inspection checklist and imagery for any nonconforming indications.  
- Traceability linking the forging to the heat lot and process route.  
All records must be retained according to Plant P3 document retention policy and be available for internal audit and customer review.

Nonconformance handling
Initial disposition
Any part or lot that fails to meet the requirements in the Requirements table shall be segregated and marked as nonconforming immediately. Do not release nonconforming parts for assembly or shipment.

Containment and evaluation
Perform containment to prevent further processing of affected material. Evaluate the extent of the nonconformance by determining if it is isolated to individual forgings or systemic across a production run. For hardness and bore tolerance failures, review the associated heat lot and die set run records to identify potential root causes. For parts exceeding the maximum forging weight of 28.4 kg, inspect the die trim and flash removal process and verify die maintenance records.

Disposition options and rationale
Acceptable dispositions include rework that demonstrably returns the part to conformance and is allowed by engineering drawing notes; controlled segregation for noncritical internal uses only if approved by engineering; or scrap. Rework that would alter the metallurgical condition (e.g., heat treatment) must be documented and validated by engineering prior to implementation. Parts that fail hardness criteria are generally not eligible for rework to meet mechanical property requirements without a documented and approved heat treatment plan. Parts exceeding the forging weight limit are often indicative of overfill and potential internal defects and must be evaluated for soundness before any rework decision.

Examples
Example of hardness failure response: a single forging reads outside 28-32 HRC at two locations. The lot is quarantined; three additional forgings from the same heat are sampled. If multiple parts are out of range, halt production, notify metallurgy, and coordinate a corrective action that may include hold, rework approval, or scrap. Record decisions and supporting test data.

Example of bore tolerance failure response: if an unmachined bore is outside ±0.10 mm, perform inspection of adjacent forgings in the run. If the issue is isolated, scrap or rework per engineering discretion; if systematic, review die fit, mandrel condition, and process parameters.

Records and corrective action
All nonconforming reports, investigation findings, root cause analyses, and corrective actions must be documented and retained with the lot quality file. Corrective actions should address immediate containment and long-term prevention, and shall include verification steps to confirm effectiveness.

Revision and control
This specification supersedes prior versions for Plant P3 production of connecting rod CFW-4516-94 (CFW-4516-94). Any deviations from this document require written engineering approval and must be recorded with justification and sign-off.
